result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Only the top of each page is visible in the screenshots, so I could not check the form, card or status message, the type and spacing scales, or the usage rules. Those scores are cautious guesses. B names its colors by job (--color-primary, canvas, surface) and states that components reference roles, not palette values, which fits the 'one edit for brand color' requirement better. A labels colors by hue scale (brand-600, ink-900) with notes on their use and shows hex values, which is readable but less clearly role-based. Both use system fonts and a calm teal tone that suits a clinic. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Only the top of each page appears in the screenshots, so I scored the sample pieces and scales mostly by inference. A names its colors by job (primary, primary soft, canvas, surface), which matches the rubric's color-by-role requirement, while B names them by hue step (brand-600, ink-900) with usage notes beside them. B shows hex values and has warmer branding (a paw mark and serif headings), but A's role-based naming makes a brand-color change one edit and is easier for a team to keep consistent.
